about: Every string guided mode's Use my own sounding card shows. Plain words in text; a CM1 name only in hint. {name} fields are filled with the file's own numbers. The sentences about one file (what is wrong with it, how it was converted, the storm such air makes, why a start is chosen) come from the gpuwm-cm1 sounding convert command, not from here.

card.line.text: Bring a sounding file of your own: a weather balloon, a forecast sounding, or one you made. GM1 checks it, shows you its air, and grows an idealized storm in it.

file.choose_help.text: Your browser reads the file, so any file you can open on this computer works, on Windows too.

file.formats.text: GM1 reads CM1's own sounding file, a University of Wyoming text listing, a SHARPpy file, or a table whose first line names its columns (pressure, height, temperature, dewpoint, wind direction and speed).

file.paste_placeholder.text: Paste the text of a sounding here

file.shipped.text: Or start from a balloon sounding GM1 ships

file.shipped_help.text: Weather balloons launched by the U.S. National Weather Service on well-known days. Use one as it is, or download it, change it and bring it back.

file.path.text: Or type the path of a file on the computer running GM1

file.wsl.text: GM1 is running under WSL, where a Windows file has another name: D:\soundings\balloon.txt is /mnt/d/soundings/balloon.txt. You can type either one here. Choose a file needs neither: it opens the Windows file picker.

file.too_large.text: That file is too large to be a sounding (over 4 MB).

file.too_large_fix.text: Choose the sounding's own text file.

file.not_read.text: Your browser could not read that file.

file.none.text: Choose a file, paste the text, or pick a sounding first.

file.empty_fix.text: Choose the file with the sounding in it.

found.read_as.text: {name}: read as {format}, {levels} levels up to {top} km above the ground.

found.converted.text: How it was converted to CM1's file

found.dropped.text: {count} line(s) of your file were left out.

found.ok.text: Nothing stops this sounding from running.

found.extend.text: Add levels up to the model top

found.extend_note.text: The added levels are made up, not measured, and the next lines say where they begin.

found.speed_kt.text: The wind speed is in knots

found.speed_ms.text: The wind speed is in metres per second

found.text_note.text: Line 1 is the ground: surface pressure in hPa, potential temperature in K, water vapour in g/kg. Each line after it is one level: height above the ground in m, potential temperature, water vapour, wind toward the east, wind toward the north.

found.kept.text: This file is kept in the run's folder when you start the storm.

preview.alt.text: Skew-T and hodograph of your sounding

preview.open.text: Open the picture full size to zoom in.

numbers.none.text: The numbers could not be worked out here: {reason}

numbers.partial.text: Worked out on the part of your file up to {top} km. Numbers that need the air above that are left out, and so is the sentence on the storm such air makes.

numbers.basis.text: Numbers for surface air, on the levels the storm will run on. A sounding at full detail gives a slightly larger instability.

numbers.motion.text: A storm in this air would move about {speed} m/s toward the {toward} (ground-relative). The view will follow it, and the next screen says the exact motion chosen and where the storm starts.

next.button.text: Next: how long can it run?

next.note.text: The next screen fits the storm to your graphics card. There you can change the grid, the area and the storm time, see the motion the view follows, and press Start.

next.waiting.text: The sounding is kept, but the storm it runs in is not in this build's gallery yet.

about.text.text: Your sounding is the air everywhere in the storm's area: flat ground, the same air on every side, nothing changing with time except the storm. It shows what kind of storm that air can make. It is not a forecast, and not a reconstruction of any real day's storms.
